prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1149; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer's narrative. On arrival at the intersection in Katy, Texas, I observed a side-impact collision between two passenger vehicles. Driver 1 was operating a sedan that had entered the intersection on a green signal when Driver 2, traveling from the cross street, struck the driver's side of the sedan. Driver 1 reported pain and swelling to the right wrist, consistent with bracing against the door or steering wheel during the impact, and was transported for evaluation. A Passenger was also present in the sedan but I was unable to establish with certainty which seat that person occupied at the moment of impact, as statements varied during the scene interview. Driver 2 stated the collision occurred as Driver 1 described, and two independent witnesses in nearby vehicles gave matching accounts. Scene photographs show intrusion and crush damage to the driver's side consistent with the reported angle of impact. Department records also show prior damage to the same area of Driver 1's vehicle from an earlier incident that was never reported to this office. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
